messages:
incident-bot: Automatic pager: elevated 5xx and increased timeouts observed on streaming endpoints in eu-central-1. Paging oncall.
alex (oncall): ack. seeing spike starting ~11:02 UTC, streaming route spawns multiple partial-frame errors and client reconnect loops. marking high-priority. @ravi @nora joining
ravi (prod-sre): checking gateway and LB. ALB target health shows healthy but connection error counts up. no large infra deploys in the past hour
nora (runtime): pulling proxy logs and http/2 traces. lots of H2 stream resets (RST_STREAM) and errors about malformed chunked encoding on the edge-to-proxy hop. sample: `HTTP/2 stream 53: RST_STREAM, code: INTERNAL_ERROR`
kai (support): support queue: three customers reporting continuous reconnects with SDKs using multiplexing. one mentioned they saw garbled JSON when reconnecting
devon (eng-runtime): initial theory: proxy emits chunked frames while upstream flush hasn't completed, and HTTP/2 multiplexing plus TCP small packets lead to interleaving causing h2 decoder to mis-interpret boundaries. Also seeing increased memory pressure on proxy from large in-flight streams
alex (oncall): quick mitigations proposal: 1) enable single-stream per connection for SDK-heavy customers (downgrade multiplex) 2) temporarily reduce max concurrent streams at gateway to reduce interleaving 3) increase keepalive timeout to allow graceful flushs 4) route heavy customers to non-streaming endpoint fallback. which to try first?
ravi (prod-sre): do 2 + 4 low-risk. reducing max-concurrent-streams at the edge is config-only and should throttle interleaving. fallback for affected customers can be applied selectively via control-plane tag
devon (eng-runtime): I'll push edge config: max_concurrent_streams=50 (was 200), connection window tweaks, and flag selective fallback for top-3 affected customers. applying canary 2% at 11:20 UTC
incident-bot: Config change: max_concurrent_streams lowered to 50 (canary 2%) by devon at 11:20 UTC
nora (runtime): telemetry after canary: H2 resets down 30% in canary, overall 5xx dropped from 14% -> 10%. memory pressure on proxy nodes still elevated; GC cycles correspond to large numbers of half-closed streams
kai (support): told customers to try non-multiplex SDK option; one customer accepted and reports fewer reconnects locally
alex (oncall): next step: identify proxy nodes with highest half-closed counts and drain them. also add targeted trace logging for chunk decoder so we can capture raw bytes around truncation events (short TTL)
devon (eng-runtime): draining node p-09 now. LB stopnew=true and lower keepalive to 15s. starting trace toggle for chunk-decoder for 30m window (will upload to telemetry bucket)
incident-bot: Node drain initiated on p-09 by devon at 11:32 UTC
ravi (prod-sre): while draining, we saw a backlog of FIN+ACK packets; kernel shows socket buffers filling. suspect application not honoring SO_LINGER or there are blocked writers. filing kernel-sock followup
nora (runtime): trace snippets: truncated-chunk header followed by immediate RST_STREAM from client, likely due to client-side cancel hitting while server-side flush partial. payloads show last bytes missing for chunk length header in some samples.
devon (eng-runtime): temporary mitigation: implement a "flush-before-close" sentinel: when proxy receives client cancel, it will delay immediate socket close for up to 50ms to allow any pending chunk bytes to be flushed to the client. patching a small behavioral change now, canary 1%
incident-bot: Deployment event: proxy-flush-sentinel v1.0 canary=1% by devon at 11:44 UTC
alex (oncall): extremely low risk; the 50ms buffer should help the race without significant latency cost. monitor p95 for additions
ora (runtime): early metrics: chunk-truncation errors in canary down 80%. overall 5xx on streaming routes down to ~3.2%. however, model-pool upstream 503 spikes persist during scale-ups; separate issue
kai (support): customer update: informing impacted customers of mitigation and suggesting SDK retries/backoff config; drafting follow-up note
devon (eng-runtime): draining finished for p-09; memory pressure relieved on that node. promoting flush-sentinel to 10% while we observe for 10m
incident-bot: Canary promotion: proxy-flush-sentinel v1.0 promoted to 10% at 11:53 UTC
ravi (prod-sre): recommend a medium-term fix: 1) unit/integration tests simulating concurrent cancel+flush, 2) ensure proxy write path is atomic for chunk frames, 3) tune model-pool autoscaler to reduce cold-start 503s. opening INF-842 for follow-ups
alex (oncall): agree. immediate action: keep flush-sentinel active, keep max_concurrent_streams reduced for now, and plan a rolling restart of 2 proxy nodes with updated socket options (TCP_NODELAY, reduced keepalive)
devon (eng-runtime): rolling restart scheduled now, one node at a time. will back out sentinel if any regressions show up
ora (runtime): note: I found a minority of traces where gzip content-encoding plus chunked framing produced slightly different chunk header sizes causing the chunk parser to expect different offsets. adding a test case for gzip+chunk interplay
kai (support): support queue update: two customers confirmed improved connectivity after switch to non-multiplex; remaining customers watching. no new high-sev tickets created
ops-lead: good coordination. once stabilized, generate an incident summary and update runbook: include SDK guidance (disable multiplexing for short-lived streams), add kernel socket tuning, and add an automated alert that correlates H2 RST_STREAM with truncated-chunk logs
alex (oncall): handing off to ops-lead for remediation follow-ups, I'll add notes to rotation log. current status: mitigated and monitoring.
incident-bot: Handoff: alex (oncall) -> ops-lead at 12:00 UTC. Incident status: mitigated, monitoring
